newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin pledges "more energetic" reforms in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin pledges "more energetic" reforms in Russia.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in a radio address on Friday that radical government changes he had started were aimed at "more energetic and consistent reforms than before".
"As you know I have recently delivered my annual address to the Federal Assembly," Yeltsin said in a clear and confident voice.

"Immediately after that first steps have been made to implement it, first of all by making changes in the government. I am talking about more energetic and consistent than before continuation of reforms."
Yeltsin has ordered Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his first deputy, reformer Anatoly Chubais, to form an effectively new government.
The new line-up of the cabinet is expected to be announced any day before Yeltsin leaves for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clintion in Helsinki next Wednesday.
